  APPROPRIATION  FOR  THE  TWEEDY  BOULEVARD  /CALIFORNIA  AVENUE
  TRAFFIC  SIGNAL  SYNCHRONIZATION  PROJECT,  PHASE n, CNTY PROJECT  NO.
  741-TRF, HSIPL 5257

  PURPOSE:  To incorporate  the Tweedy  Boulevard/Califoinia  Avenue  Traffic Signal
  Synchronizat'ion Phase II Project to the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Capital Improvement Program, and
  appropriate funding for it.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTTONS:  The City Council will consider:
  (a) Amending the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Capital Improvement Progran"i to add in the Tweedy
  Boulevard/California Avenue Ttaffic Signal Synchtonization Phase II, City Project No,
  74'l-TRP, HSIP 5257; and,
  (b) Appropriating  $100,000  in Proposition  C Funds to the Tweedy  Boulevard/California
  Avenue Traffic Signal Synchronization  Project Phase II, City Project No. 741-TRP, HSIP
  5257, as necessary to fund the preparation of plans, specifications and estimates (PS&E).

  FISCAL J)%/IPACT: There is no impact on the General Fund. The proposed appropriation  is in
  the amount of $100,000 in Proposition C Funds.

  ANALYSNS:  The City received a $958,800 Highway  Safety Improvement  Prograna (HSIP)
  Grant from Caltrans to fund the Tweedy Boulevard Signal Synchronization  Phase II Project, The
  Project aims to improve pedestrian and veliicular safety and relieve traffic congestion on the
  boulevard. More specifically, the project will syncbronize the remaitiing 7 traffic signals along
  (a) Tweedy Boulevard, between Alameda Street and Victoria Avenue, and (b) along California
  Avenue, between Tweedy Boulevard and City Hall.  The grant monies will fund installing
  conduit and fiber optic cabling to physically connect the traffic signals to each other, as well as
  to upgrade the existing traffic signal cabinets and controllers,  In light of the grant funds
  received, the City Council may now amend the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Capital Improvement
  Program to add in the Tweedy  Boulevard/California  Avenue  Traffic  Signal  Synchronization
  Phase n.

  The HSIP Grant includes a local match requirement,  meariing the City must contribute  a poition
  of the project  cost  in the  amount  of  $100,000.  Accordingly,  City  Council  approval  is

  I

  565
 recommended  to appropriate  $100,000  in Proposition  C Funds  to satisfy  the required  local  match
contribution.  These  funds  will  be used  to support  the design  phase  of the project,  including
engineering  design  services,  staff time,  and project  management.

BACKGROUND:  Tweedy  Boulevard  is a vital  arterial  in the City's  roadway  network,  serving
a major  commercial  corridor  including  the Tweedy  Mile  district,  as well  as providing  access to
schools  and  surrounding  residential  neighborhoods.  The  corridor  carries  over  24,000  daily
vehicle  trips  along  a segment  with  closely  spaced signalized  intersections,  resulting  in congestion
and traffic  circulation  challenges.  As a first-phase  effort  towards  improving  conditions,  a traffic
signal  synchronization  system  was installed  on Tweedy  Boulevard  between  Victoria  Avenue  and
Atlantic  Avenue.  The  synchronization  system  served  to improve  traffic  flow,  reduce  vehicle
delays  and travel  times,  enhance  intersection  operations,  and improve  overall  corridor  efficiency
and safety.

The  Tweedy  Boulevard/California  Avenue  Traffic  Signal  Synchronization  is  a proposal  to
expand  upon  the traffic  signal  synchronization  along  both  Tweedy  Boulevard  and California
Avenue.  On Tweedy  Boulevard,  synchronization  will  be implemented  from  Alameda  Avenue  to
Victoria  Avenue,  and  on California  Avenue,  synchronization  will  be installed  from  Tweedy
Boulevard  to City  Hall.  The proposed  improvements  will  help  create  a more  coordinated  and
efficient  traffic  network,  improving  mobility  and reducing  congestion  along  two  of the City's
major  arterial  corridors.

Design  is anticipated  to begin  June 2026,  and be completed  within  five  (5) months,  allowing  the
project  to proceed  into the construction  phase.

  LNGHTING  :FOR REPAIRS  TO HIGff  VOLT  AGF,  SERIES  STREETLNGHT  CIRCUITS
  N0. 24 AND N0. 27

  PURPOSE:  To approve  a Purchase  Order  with  California  Street Lighting,  for repairs  to High
  Voltage Series Streetlight Circuits No. 24, located  near Duane Avenue  and Virginia  Avenue,  and
  No. 27, located near Adella Avenue.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTNONS:  The City Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  a Purchase  Order  with  California  Street Lighting,  on a sole-source  basis, for
  repairs to High Voltage  Series Streetlight  Circuits  No. 24, located near Duane Avenue  and
  Virginia  Avenue,  ai"id No. 27, located  near Adella  Avenue,  in an amount  not to exceed
  $133,250;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to execute the Purchase  Order,  in a form  approved  by the
  City Attorney,

  FISCALI!VIPACT:  ThereisnoimpactontheGeneralFund.TheproposedPurchaseOrderisin
  the amount of $133,250, and it will be funded with $66,625  in Gas Tax Funds  and $66,625  in
  Measure R Funds, budgeted for the Fiscal Year 2025/26.

  ANALYSIS:  The City's  streetlight  system includes  aging series high voltage  circuits  that require
  specialized  maintenance  and repair expertise.  Circuits  No. 24 and No. 27 are experiencing  outages
  affecting  multiple  stteetlights  and reducing  nighttime  visibility  andpublic  safety withinresidential
  areas. Prompt  restoration  of street lighting  circuits  is necessm'y to maintain  public  safety, traffic
  visibility,  and pedestrian  security.

  The Public  Works  Electrical  Division  continues  to address ongoiiig  streetlight  maintenance  and
  outage repairs  citywide;  however,  limited  staffing  levels  combined  with  multiple  street lighting
  system issues have increased  the need for specialized  contractor  support.  Due to the volume  and
  complexity  of current  system repairs,  staff determined  that supplemental  contractor  services  are
  necessary to restore lighting  service in a timely  and efficient  manner.

  I

  567
 California  Street  Lighting  has  extensive  experience  performing  repairs  and maintenance  on
municipal  street lighting  systems,  including  specialized  high voltage  series circuits  similar  to those
operated  by the City.  The contractor  currently  provides  comparable  services  for multiple  public
agencies  and  has  demonstrated  the  technical  capability,  operational  readiness,  and  staffing
necessary  to perform  these repairs  efficiently  and safely.

Staff recommend  utilizing  California  Street Lighting  on a sole-source  basis due to the contractor's
ability  to immediately  mobilize  qualified  personnel  and equipment  upon issuance  of the Purchase
Order.  Timely  response  is critical  because  prolonged  streetlight  outages  create  public  safety
concerns  and may  increase  liability  exposure  to the City.  The  specialized  nature  of the City's
remaining  series  lighting  infrastructure  further  limits  the  availability  of qualified  contractors
capable  of performing  this work.

Pursuing  a formal  competitive  procurement  process  would  likely  delay repairs  and restoration  of
lighting  service  without  providing  significant  additional  benefit  to the City.  California  Street
Lighting's  familiarity  with  municipal  streetlight  systems  and ability  to respond  immediately  will
minimize  service  interniptions,  reduce  operational  risks,  and ensure  compliance  with  applicable
electrical  and safety  standards.

Therefore,  staff recommends  approval  of the Purchase  Order  with  California  Street Lighting  in an
amount  not to exceed  $133,250  for repairs  to Series High  Voltage  Street Light  Circuits  No. 24 and
No. 27.

BACKGROUND:  The  City  maintains  approximately  4,400  streetlights  throughout  the
coinrnunity  that  are powered  through  72 streetlight  circuits.  Approximately  45 percent  of the
system  has been upgraded  to LED  lighting,  while  the remaining  portions  of the system  continue
to operate  on older  high voltage  series circuits  utilizing  incandescent  lighting  technology.  Due to
the age and configuration  of the existing  series  system,  these  circuits  are more  susceptible  to
outages  and require  specialized  repair  services.

Streetlight  outages  may occur  due to technical  failures,  Southern  California  Edison  (SCE)  power
interruptions,  vandalism,  underground  electrical  faults,  or failed  lighting  components.  Depending
on the nature ofthe  outage,  impacts  may range from  isolated  streetlight  failures  to outages  affecting
an  entire  circuit  and multiple  streets.

The Public  Works  Electrical  Division  provides  ongoing  oversight,  maintenance,  and repair  of the
City's  streetlight  system  and works  to restore  outages  as quickly  as possible.  However,  repairs
involving  high voltage  series circuits  can be complex  and may require  specialized  contractors  due
to the technical  expertise,  equipment,  and staffing  necessary  to safely  diagnose  and complete
repairs.  In addition,  limited  staffing  resources  and the increasing  number  of systemwide  streetlight
issues have created  a need for supplemental  contractor  assistance  to address  outages  in a timely
manner.  Repairing  timelines  may range  from  several  days to multiple  weeks  depending  on the
extent  of the damage  and the complexity  of the electrical  issues involved.

Series  High  Voltage  Street  Light  Circuits  No.  24,  located  near  Duane  Avenue  and Virginia
Avenue,  and No. 27, located  near Adella  Avenue,  currently  require  specialized  repairs  to restore

 lighting  service  in the  affected  areas.  Staff  evaluated  available  options  and determined  that
California  Street Lighting  is best qualified  to perform  the necessary  repairs  in a timely  and reliable
manner.

 BANK, N.A. FOR BANKING  SERVICF,S

PURPOSE: To approve a Professional Services Agreement with BMO Bank, N.A. ("Bank") to provide
banking services to the City of South Gate.

RECOMMF,NDF,D  ACTNONS: The City Council will consider:
  a, Approving a Professional Services Agreement with BMO Bank, N.A. for a period of five (5) years,
  with up to five (5) one-yearextensionsat the Cit31s sole discretion,for a total term not to exceed
  ten (10) years; and
  b. Authorize the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form approved by the City Attoxney

FNSCAL NMPACT: Underthe proposedAgreement, the City is projectedto incur no out-of-pocket banking
service charges and to generate approximately $91,209 per year in new interest income, for an estimated
netpositive annual impact of approximately $91,000 to $120,000 compared to the prior arrangetnent.  Upon
execution, the Bank will also provide a one-tie  Loyalty Credit of $25,000 and waive account analysis
service charges for the first six (6) months, representing additional one-time savings of approximately
$29,885. No new General Fund appropriation is requested, and sufficient appropriations are included in the
City's adopted budget.

Estimated annual service charges are approximately $59,771 (approximately $4,981 per month), based on
the City's historical transaction volumes, Unit pricing is fixed for the initial five-year term, Service charges
are offset monthly through an Earnings Ctedit Rate (ECR) of three and five-hundredths percent (3.05%)
applied to tlie City's average collected balances, subject to a O.30% floor. Appliedto an illustrative average
collected balance of$5,000,000, the ECR generates approximately $152,500 in annual earnings credit, more
tlian sufficient to fily offsetthe City's estimated annual service charges. For balances held above the level
required to offset fees, the Bank provides an interest-bearing Hybrid account paying 3.00% per annun; on
the same $5,000,000 illustative balance, the remaining approximately $3,040,000 in the Hybrid account
would generate approximately $7,601 per month, or $91,209 annually. The ECR aiid Hybrid rate are bank-
managed and subject to market conditiorhs, with thirty (30) days' prior written notice of any change. Actual
balaxtces will varyy; the figures above are illustrative and not guaranteed.

EXECUTIVE  SUMMARY:  Following a competitive procurement process (Request for Proposals No,
FIN-2026-01),  staff recommends awarding a Professional Services Agreement to BMO Bank, N,A.., to

  l
  572
 serve as the City's primary depository and treasury management institution. The Agreement provides for an
initial five-year term with up to five one-year renewal options, fixed unit pricing, an Earnings Credit Rate
of 3.05% to offset service charges, a Hybrid account paying 3.00% on excess balances, a one-time $25,000
Loyalty Credit, and a six-month waiver of account analysis service charges. The Agreement incorporates
the City's required insurance, indemnification,  cybersecurity, data-residency, and audit provisions, and
establishes a clear order of precedence under which the City's Agreement and Request for Proposals
supersede the Bank's standard treasury and account terms.

BACKGROUND:  On May 24, 2016, the City Council approved Contract No. 3218 with Bank of the West
to provide banking services for an initial ternn of five (5) years, with up to five one-year renewal options.
On February 1, 2023, Bank of the West became BMO Bank, N.A. through a formal acquisition  that
transferred its business deposit and cash management operations. Amendments Nos. 1 through 3 exercised
the available renewal options and extended the agreement through December 31, 2025, and a subsequent
six-month extension carried the agreement through June 30, 2026, to align with completion  of the
competitive  procurement  process.

The City issued Request for Proposals No. FIN-2026-01 for Banking Services on February 26, 2026, in
accordance with the City's purchasing policies and California public agency procurement requirements.
Proposals were received by the April 6, 2026 deadline, and evaluated by a staff review committee.
Following the evaluation, BMO Bank, N.A., was determined to provide the best overall value to the City.

ANALYSIS:  The Agreement  consolidates the City's banking, depository, disbursement,  electronic
payment, fraud prevention, account reconciliation, and reporting services with a single financial institution,
supporting operational efficiency and a unified earnings credit framework. Required controls  include
Positive Pay with Payee Validation, dual authorization, multi-factor  authentication for wire and ACH
origination, encryption of City data in transit and at rest, twenty-four-hour  security monitoring, U.S.-based
data residency, and defined incident notification timelines. The Bank is required to maintain a documented
business continuity and disaster recovery program.

Service performance is supported by a dedicated relationship management team, online reporting with audit
trails, monthly account analysis statements, and the retention of transaction records for 7 years. Because
BMO is the incumbent institution, the City does not anticipate a full system conversion; the Agreement
nonetheless preserves the City's rights to a coordinated implementation plan and orderly disentanglement
support at the end of the term.

The Agreement establishes an order of precedence under which the executed Professional Services
Agreement controls, followed by the City's RFP, the Bank's proposal, and the Bank's standard treasury and
account terms. This structure ensures that the City's specifications, indemnification, insurance, audit, data-
protection, and termination provisions take precedence over the Bank's standard-form documents.

Legal  Authority  and  Compliance

The Agreement is structured in compliance with California Government Code Sections 53630 through
53686 governing the deposit and security of local agency fiinds, including collateralization of deposits at
not less than 110 percent of City balances above the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation  (FDIC)
coverage. BMO Bank, N.A. is a qualified public depository under Government Code Section 53649, is a
member of the Federal Reserve System, and is insured by the FDIC. The Agreement is consistent  with the

  2
  573
 South  Gate Municipal  Code procurement  provisions  at Section  1.54.320  et seq. and has been reviewed  by
the City Attorney's  Office.

Staff  recommends  that the City  Council  approve  the Professional  Services  Agreement  with  BMO  Bank,
N.A.  for Banking  Services  and authorize  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  in a form  approved  as to
foim  by the City Attorney.

  RECIT  ALS

  WHEREAS,  the  City  desires  to  retain  a qualified  financial  institution  to  provide
  comprehensive  banking  services  for the City's  operating,  payroll,  and special-purpose  accounts,
  including  general  depository,  treasury  management,  disbursement,  electronic  payment,  account
  analysis,  and related  services  in compliance  with  California  law governing  the deposit  and security
  of public  funds;  and

  WHEREAS,  the City issued Request  for Proposals  No. FIN-2026-01  for Banking  Services
  on February  26, 2026,  and conducted  a competitive  procurement  process  pursuant  to which  the
  City  evaluated  proposals  received  and selected  Contractor  as the proposer  offering  the best overall
  value to the City;  and

  WHEREAS,  Contractor  warrants  to  City  that  it has the  requisite  skills,  knowledge,
  qualifications,  manpower,  and expertise  to perform  properly  and timely  the Professional  Services
  under this Agreement;  and

  WHEREAS,  based on such representation,  the City  desires  to contract  with  Contractor  to
  perform  the services  as described  in the Scope of Services  attached  hereto  as Exhibit  "A"  of this
  Agreement.

  NOW,  THEREFORE,  the Parties  hereby  agree as follows:

  engagement,  to perform  banking  services  as set forth  in the Scope  of Services  described  in the
  City's  Request  for Proposals  No.  FIN-2026-01  for Banking  Services,  attached  hereto  as Exhibit
  "A"  and incorporated  herein  by reference,  and Contractor's  proposal  dated April  6, 2026, attached
  hereto  as  Exhibit  "B"  and  incorporated  herein  by  reference,  together  with  all  material
  representations,  commitments,  and service  levels  contained  in Contractor's  proposal  submitted  in

  terms  and conditions  and treasury  management  service  agreements  applicable  to the  services
  rendered  hereunder  are attached  hereto  as Exhibit  "C"  and incorporated  herein  by reference,

 1. Overview

1.I Purpose
The City of South  Gate  (City)  invites  qualified  financial  institutions  to submit  proposals  to
provide  secure,  efficient,  and innovative  banking  and related  services  in accordance  with
this RFP.  The  City seeks  to establish  a five-year  agreement  with up to Five optional  one-
year  extensions,  subject  to satisfactory  performance  and  City  Council  approval.  The
selected  institution  will  safeguard  public  funds,  enhance  liquidity  management,  and
support  operational  efficiency  in compliance  with State  and Federal  law.

1.2 Background
The City of South  Gate was  incorporated  on January  20, 1923  under  the general  laws of
the  State  of California.  South  Gate  encompasses  7.49  square  miles  and  is located  in
the  heart  of  the  Los  Angeles  Metropolitan  area  approximately  10  miles  south  of
downtown  Los  Angeles.  Services  provided  by the  City  include  administration,  public
works,  planning  and  building,  police,  and  parks  and  recreation.  As of 2025,  the  City's
population  is  approximately  96,547.  The  population  of  this  working  class  city  is
predominately  Latino  and overwhelmingly  young  with  nearly  one-third  of the  population
under  the age of 18 years.

Centrally  located,  South  Gate  is an  ideal  location  for  commerce  with  downtown  Los
Angeles,  Los  Angeles  International  Airport,  and  the  Ports  of Los  Angeles  and  Long
Beach  all within  a 15-mile  radius.  The  City has a diverse  mix of residential,  commercial
and industrial  areas.

The  City  has  a council-manager  form  of government.  Policy-making  and  legislative
authority  are  vested  in the  governing  City  Council,  which  consists  or five  Council
Members,  including  the Mayor  and Mayor  Pro-Tem.  The City Manager  is responsible  for
carrying  out the  policies  and  ordinances  of the City  Council,  for overseeing  the day-to-
day operations  of the City,  and for appointing  the heads  of the City's  departments.  The
City Council  is elected  on a non-partisan,  at-large  basis.  Council  Members  are elected  to
four-year  staggered  terms  with two or three  Council  Members  elected  every  two years.

The  City  of South  Gate  currently  maintains  a primary  commercial  banking  relationship
with  one  depository  institution.  It is the  City's  preference  to  maintain  all commercial
banking  services  with  one  financial  institution  to  maximize  cash  flow  and  minimize
administrative  costs.  The  City  encourages  financial  institutions  to  submit  the  most
comprehensive  proposal  possible  offering  the  highest  quality  of service  while  providing
opportunities  for  improving  the  current  management  of cash  flow.  The  City  is also
interested  in  various  technological  advances  that  could  improve  banking,  cash
management,  and customer  service  capabilities.

1.3 0bjectives
  Secure  a financially  sound,  service-oriented  public  depository.
  Consolidate  banking  relationships  while  maintaining  strong  internal  controls.
  Improve  cash  management  and electronic  service  capabilities.
  Ensure  full compliance  with all laws governing  public  deposits.

  PURPOSE:  California  Governrnent  Code Section 53646 requires staff to submit a report to the
  City Council and City Manager,  at least quarterly,  which provides  detailed  infornnation  on all
  investments of the City.

  RECO1%4ME!%TDED ACTION:  The City Council will consider receiving  and filing  the Quarterly
  Investment Report for the quarter ended March 31, 2026.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Interest earnings totaled $296,917.65  fot the quarter.

  ANALYSIS:  See Executive  Summary  and Background  mid Analysis  sections below.

  EXE,CUTTVE  SUMMARY:  As of March 31, 2026, the City's investment portfolio  totaled
  $96,898,684 at cost and $96,968,528 at market value. The portfolio generated $296,917.65 in
  interest earnings during the quarter and remains fully compliatit with the City's Inyestment Policy
  and California Government Code Section 53600 et seq. Investments have an average credit rating
  of AA- and are structured to preserve capital, ensure sufficient liquidity for operational needs, and
  deliver a reasonable rate of return witthose  constraints, There are no compliance issues, credit
  concerns, or Iiquidity  constraints to report. The portfolio  continues to perform as intended,
  providing stable earnings while maintaining sufficient liquidity to support City operations.

  While investment  earnings providc a meaningful  supplemental revenue source, the portfolio is
  managed primarily  to ensure the safety and availability of public funds. It is not intended to offset
  the City's ongoing  structural imbalance between reveniies and expenditures.

  BACKGROUND  AND  ANALYSJ[S:  California  Government  Code Section  53646  requires
  qumterly  repotts to the City Council  detailing  inyesttnent  activity  and portfolio  status.

  This report provides  the City Council  with a current snapshot of the City's investment  holdings,
  liquidity  position,  and compliance  with  applicable  laws and policies  as of March  31, 2026.

  634
 Attachments  include  detailed  investment  listings,  cash balances,  and prior-quarter  reports  for
reference.

Consistent  with  the City's  broader  financial  reporting,  this report  reflects  the City's  position  at a
point  in time.  It should  be considered  alongside  the City's  budget  and multi-year  financial  outlook,
which  address the sustainability  of ongoing  operations.

Attached  is the Investment  Report  for the quarter  ending  March  31, 2026, for the City  and Housing
Authority  (Attachment  A).  This  submission  provides  the latest  available  valuation  of the City's
investment  portfolio  and apprises  the City  Council  of the City's  financial  position  as of the end of
the third  quarter  of FY 2025-26.

Portfolio  Overview
The  portfolio  is invested  in high-quality,  fixed-income  instruments  consistent  with  the  City's
conservative  investment  policy.  As of March  31, 2026,  the portfolio  was allocated  as follows:
31.04%  in U.S.  Treasuries  ($30,078,885);  18.21%  in corporate  bonds  ($17,642,467);  17.98%  in
LAIF  ($17,420,645);  13.88%  in  mortgage-backed  securities  ($13,449,518);  8.94%  in  U.S.
agencies  ($8,658,015);  8.83%  in cornrnercial  paper  ($8,559,666);  0.77%  in negotiable  certificates
of deposit  ($744,000);  and O.36% in a money  market  fund  ($345,488).  The average  credit  rating
of securities  held in U.S.  Bank  safekeeping  was AA-.  The total  portfolio  balance  increased  from
$96.5 million  on December  31, 2025, to $96.9 million  as of March  31, 2026.

The  City's  composition  of  investments  has  substantially  changed  since  the  last  quarterly
investment  report  on December  31, 2025, due to the hiring  of the investment  management  services
firm,  Meeder  Public  Funds.  Upon  execution  of the agreement  in March  2026,  Meeder  acted
quickly  to purchase  several  securities  on the City's  behalf  to diversify  holdings  and lock in longer-
term rates, hedging  against  potential  market  fluctuations  driven  by unknown  future  conditions  and
external  market  forces.

Liquidity  and Maturity  Profile
The  City's  maturity  distribution  has changed  since  the previous  quarter.  The  City  now  holds
investments  that will  mature  at various  time  intervals,  including  16.6%  within  4-5 years,  16.3%
within  3-4 years, 15.8%  within  2-3 years, 14.1%  within  1-2 years, 18.8%  within  1 year, and 18.3%
available  the  same  day.  Same-day  investments  are primarily  composed  of  the  City's  LAIF
holdings,  with  a small  portion  held  in a money  market  fund.  Prior  to Meeder's  hiring,  the City
maintained  a highly  liquid  posture,  with  money  market  and LAIF  positions  combined  representing
85.32%  of the portfolio  ($82,352,417).

Investment  Performance
The City's  investment  portfolio  earned  $296,918  in interest  during  the quarter  ended  March  31,
2026  (Q3  FY  2025-26).  In  contrast,  total  earnings  for  Q2  FY  2025-26  (the  quarter  ending
December  31, 2025)  were  $821,583.  This  reduction  does not reflect  underperformance  of the
portfolio,  but rather atemporary  reduction  in reported  income  due to a large volume  of transactions
processed  by Meeder  Public  Funds  in their  first month  as investment  manager  for the City.

  635
  2#
 Specifically,  Meeder  made  investments  on behalf  of the City  totaling  nearly  $70 million.  As part
of these  transactions,  the previous  bondholders  (sellers  of the  securities)  were  paid  the accrued
interest  owed  to them  up to the date of settlement.  When  each investment  reaches  its next  semi-
annual  coupon  date, the City  will  receive  the full  six-month  coupon  payment  despite  having  owned
the  security  for  only  a  portion  of  the  coupon  period.  The  accrued  interest  paid  totaled
approximately  $418,000,  materially  reducing  the reportable  interest  income  for the quarter.

Because  the shift  in investment  strategy  with  Meeder's  assistance  began  only  in March,  the impact
on earnings  will  be more  visible  in 'future  periods.  On an annualized  basis,  the updated  investment
composition  is projected  to yield approximately  $2.76 million  in FY 2026-27.

Policy  Compliance
All  investments  held  during  the quarter  were  made  in full  compliance  with  the City's  Investment
Policy  and  California  Governrnent  Code  Sections  53600  through  53607.  Per policy,  maximum
maturity  is five years.  No exceptions,  violations,  or credit  events  were  identified  during  the quarter.
Staff  certifies  that the City  has sufficient  cash flow  from  maturing  investments  and liquid  :funds to
meet  all anticipated  expenditures  for the next  six months.

  Pursuant  to Government  Code Section  54956.9(a),  54954.9(b)(3)(c),
  54956.9(d)(1)(4)

  a.  Robert  Mendoza  vs COSG
  b.  Jonathan  Dominic  Aguilar  vs COSG,  et al.
  c.  Southern  California  Edison  Company  vs Various  Counties

  On item 2(a), the city received  a report  with  respect  to a potential
  resolution  on that matter.  On a motion  made by Council  Member  Hurtado
  and seconded  by Mayor  Barron,  City  Council  moved  to approve  a
  tentative  settlement  on that matter.  The vote was 4-1, with  Council
  Member  Rios abstaining  from that decision.

  Item 2(b) involves  a car versus car accident  on Tweedy  Boulevard  near
  Truba Avenue  in the year 2024. After  a presentation  by the City Attorney,
  the City  Council  made a motion  to retain  counsel  to defend  that matter.
  The motion  was made by Councilwoman  Davila  and seconded  by Council
  Member  Hurtado  and the vote was 5-0.

  Item 2(c) is a claim  by Southern  California  Edison  against  the State Board
  of Equalization  including  several  counties  and cities in the state. The
  allegation  in the complaint  is that the properties  that are owned  by Edison
  were appraised  at a higher  value than their  worth.  Edison  is seeking  to
  recover  the over appraisal  of those properties.  By law, they are required  to
  notify  any of the affected  agencies  that may have received  revenue  from
  that over appraisal.  South Gate is one of those along with  many  other
  cities  in the respective  counties  that are involved.  The City  of South  Gate
  was given  the opportunity  to actively  participate  in this or to monitor  this
  matter  without  active  participation.  There  was a motion  made by Vice
  Mayor  Rios not to intervene  in the action  but to monitor  the case very
  closely  and seconded  by Mayor  Barron.  The vote was 5-O to agree with
  Vice Mayor  Rios'  motion.
